neighbours.label: The word 'and' joining a famous pair of names into one fixed name, strongest for old showbiz, explorer and brand pairs (Barnum and Bailey, Laurel and Hardy, Simon and Garfunkel), lighting up on the 'and' itself; quiet on 'and' between ordinary names or things (two neighbours' surnames, two foods). Patchy: some famous pairs (Romeo and Juliet, Tom and Jerry, Marx and Engels) stay quiet. It also lights up on the piece that completes a famous multi-part title or name (Edwin Drood).
neighbours.short: 'and' inside a famous name pair (Barnum and Bailey)
neighbours.notes: Step-in reader of L29/N7840- (drop 0.05, second-largest; the largest, L35/N10152+, already has a record). Little to do with the feeder's instrument/sports-part meaning. Top corpus examples are a mixed bag (mid-compound CJK characters, mid-word pieces, 'and' in Barnum and Bailey, 'the' in Order of the Golden Dawn). Strongest feeder L27/N5995- fires on mid-word pieces of katakana/Hangul words. Test sentences written blind by a second author from the label only.
fire: Synopsis of the musical The Mystery of Edwin Drood.
The circus posters proudly advertised Barnum and Bailey as the greatest show on earth.
We spent the rainy afternoon watching old Laurel and Hardy shorts.
My dad still plays Simon and Garfunkel records every Sunday morning.
The expedition of Lewis and Clark mapped vast stretches of the American West.
She bought a new jar of mustard at the Marks and Spencer food hall.
Abbott and Costello made the 'Who's on First?' routine famous.
The detergent aisle was dominated by brands from Procter and Gamble.
quiet: My neighbours Smith and Jones share a fence.
The circus posters proudly advertised the clowns as the greatest show on earth.
We spent the rainy afternoon watching old silent comedy shorts.
My dad still plays his folk records every Sunday morning.
The early expedition mapped vast stretches of the American West.
She bought a jar of mustard and a loaf of bread at the shop.
My cousins Peter and Laura told jokes at the family dinner.
The detergent aisle was full of bottles and boxes in bright colours.
